title: Telluride School District talks housing developments
copy: The Telluride School District is working with Rural Homes and CHFA to expand housing options for employees, with 20 units planned at Two Rivers and additional rentals in Rico and behind the middle/high school. A CHFA program cuts mortgage rates roughly in half — from around 7.7% to 3.5% — with down payment assistance available. The district held information sessions this month so employees could learn about the options and ask questions.

title: THS takes winning ways to Ridgway
copy: Telluride High School beat Ridgway 4-2 on the road, staying unbeaten in league play at 10-1-0. Montano, Clarke (two), and Zago Carolei scored for the Miners, with Young and Slosberg each making nine and seven saves respectively. THS hosts Coal Ridge next Saturday at 11 a.m.

title: A clothing drive with heart
copy: Telluride Storage at 650 S. Park Rd. is running its third annual winter clothing drive through Oct. 27, collecting coats, gloves, hats, boots, and other cold-weather gear via a 24/7 drop box out front. Donated items go to organizations across the region, including Navajo Nation, Ute Mountain Ute Tribe, and Haven House.

title: Connecting invisible threads
copy: Devaki Murch, a survivor of the 1975 Operation Babylift plane crash, brings her traveling exhibit *My Name is Mimosa* to The Livery in Norwood on Oct. 24 at 7 p.m. She's been reconnecting adoptees, volunteers, and others tied to the airlift using 33 boxes of documents discovered in a nun's basement. Free, open to the public.

title: CHALKBOARD week of Oct. 15-21
copy: The Chalkboard for Oct. 15–21 lists birthdays for 14 locals and runs through recurring community meetings and services in Norwood and the Nucla-Naturita area. Regular fixtures include the Food Pantry, Senior Meals, Free Legal Aid, and pickleball. The Farmers Market runs Thursdays through mid-October.

title: Correction, apology regarding a letter to the editor
copy: The Telluride Times has issued a correction and apology after a letter to the editor incorrectly claimed sheriff's office license-plate-reader accounts were canceled the day before a public records request arrived — the CORA request actually came two days earlier, and account updates were routine policy and personnel maintenance. The paper's own investigation found the allegations unsubstantiated.

title: With anger spreading over Iran war, Democrats hope to flip Republican seats with veterans' help
copy: Democrats are putting money into Colorado's heavily military 5th Congressional District for the first time in years, backing veteran Jessica Killin against Republican Rep. Jeff Crank. Some longtime Republican veterans in the district say the Iran war and Pentagon leadership have them reconsidering their usual vote.

title: Arizona State hires veteran NHL coach Dave Hakstol to lead program, Powers announces resignation
copy: Arizona State hired former NHL head coach Dave Hakstol to lead its hockey program after coach Greg Powers resigned amid an investigation into a workout that left 21-year-old player Matthew Mayich on life support with severe heat stroke. An independent review led by a former state Supreme Court chief justice is ongoing, with findings expected by early December. Hakstol previously coached the Flyers, Kraken, and North Dakota.

title: Everyone has the same question in the midterms — where's the beef? (And how much does it cost?)
copy: Beef has become a recurring campaign theme in this midterm cycle, with candidates in Mississippi, Colorado, Iowa, Texas, and Arizona all fielding attacks or making moves around meat-eating and agricultural policy. Ground beef is running around $6.79 a pound nationally, up from $5.55 in January. Both parties are working the issue, though from different angles.

title: Green Grants program expands to the West End
copy: EcoAction Partners' Green Grants program has expanded into the West End of Montrose County, backed by roughly $85,000 from the Telluride Foundation. Grants typically run $5,000–$10,000 and can go toward heat pumps, windows, and EV infrastructure. The intent-to-apply deadline is October 30 at telluride-co.gosmart.org.

title: We're on the edge of our seats
copy: The Telluride Horror Show runs October 16–18 for its 17th year, with headliners including Universal's upcoming slasher *River* and *Victorian Psycho*. Several films have local ties, including *The Cycle*, which features Telluride's own Jeb Berrier. Free screenings, campfire readings, and library films round out the weekend.

title: Legals and Public Notices for Oct. 15-21, 2026
copy: Sawpit's Board of Trustees will review the town's proposed 2027 budget at a public meeting November 19 at 6:30PM. Separately, a Tomboy Lodge unit at 619 W Columbia Ave is headed to foreclosure sale in San Miguel County, and Good Gargoyle Condominiums mortgage holders are being notified of a proposed declaration amendment.

title: Amendment 83 is a trap, vote No
copy: A Colorado veterinarian of 23 years is urging a No vote on Amendment 83, arguing that while it's framed as protecting hunting and fishing rights — already legal in Colorado — it would enshrine "traditional methods" in the state Constitution. She says supporters have acknowledged this language could revive steel-jawed traps, neck snares, and poisons that voters banned in 1996.

title: 5A prevents devastating cuts
copy: Telluride schools are facing a double financial hit — declining enrollment means less state funding, and Colorado's new formula also cuts per-student dollars. Ballot Issue 5A would use local property taxes to partially offset those state reductions, though per-student funding would still drop even if it passes. Without it, programs like Dual Immersion, sports, and student support services are on the table.

title: Writing in support of 5A
copy: Telluride R-1's Ballot Issue 5A would raise property taxes roughly $117 per year per $1M assessed value to offset state funding cuts tied to a revised school finance formula. Under the new formula, the district could lose around 17% per-pupil funding — enough to threaten programs. The measure won't close the gap entirely, but would soften the impact.

title: Support continued excellence
copy: Telluride School District ranks in Colorado's top 10% and performs well nationally, but faces a funding squeeze — state per-student funding is down 17% and costs keep climbing. San Miguel County sits near the bottom in Colorado for property tax rates, around half the national average. Ballot Measure 5A would raise those rates to help close the gap.

title: Democrat Lane Masters for sheriff
copy: Lane Masters, a Telluride native and Marine veteran, is running for San Miguel County Sheriff as a Democrat. He brings 13 years in law enforcement — including homicide and bomb squad work in Bismarck — plus a degree in emergency management. He opposes ALPRs and ICE cooperation; incumbent Dan supports both.

title: Vote No on Amendment 81
copy: A local resident writes to oppose Amendment 81, which would permanently change the Colorado Constitution to require state and local law enforcement to notify ICE when someone is charged — before any conviction. The writer argues this conflicts with existing state laws limiting ICE authority and raises due process concerns.

title: Ghost Stories
copy: A writer reflects on growing up in an 1820 Maine farmhouse where ghostly figures — a woman in a black hat, a restless child, a man in overalls — were regular presences. The experiences passed to the next generation when her young daughter encountered a spirit at the staircase. The family treated it all as a matter of course.

title: The Times they are a-changin' (again)
copy: The Telluride Daily Planet, bought by Hoffmann Media Group in fall 2025 and renamed The Telluride Times, is now shifting to management under Lee Enterprises, which HMG's owner recently acquired. Starting with the Oct. 29 print edition, readers will notice some layout and sizing changes, though staff, coverage, and familiar features stay the same. The horoscope column is temporarily on hold due to an unrelated subscription issue.

title: Bright sparks
copy: Students at Telluride Middle/High School got a look at the Sparky Scholarship program this week, as board members — including founder Jennie Franks — held their first monthly luncheon of the year. The program, part of True North Youth Program, focuses on academic success and college access. Future applicants are welcome to join upcoming luncheons.

title: October is Domestic Violence Awareness Month
copy: Purple ribbons are going up around the region this month, courtesy of San Miguel Resource Center staff and volunteers marking Domestic Violence Awareness Month. Residents and businesses can call SMRC to get ribbons for their own doors, fences, and windows.

title: I measure return on investment for a living. The math says 'yes' on 5A
copy: Ballot Issue 5A would partially offset a projected $3 million annual drop in state school funding, which the district estimates could eliminate 33–65 positions over five years. The cost to property owners works out to roughly $115 a year per $1 million of assessed value. This guest commentary, written by a local parent and ROI professional, makes the financial case for passing the measure.

title: Good, better, best
copy: The "optimization" trend has saturated daily life — sleep, protein, dopamine, creativity, all of it. Neuroscience is pushing back, showing the brain actually needs boredom and blank space to function well. Worth sitting with before adding whey protein to your soup.

title: Open enrollment is coming
copy: Colorado's Open Enrollment for 2027 health plans runs Nov. 1 through Jan. 15. Enroll by Dec. 15 for Jan. 1 coverage. Thrive Community Health Network offers free, bilingual help — including a local event at Wilkinson Public Library Oct. 15, 4–6 p.m. Call (970) 708-7096.

title: Gondola operating dates extended throughout the next year
copy: The gondola's operating calendar is getting stretched at both ends. This fall it runs through Oct. 25, a week later than usual, and next summer it opens May 20 — also a week early. TMVOA is covering the added costs and pairing the extra days with events.

title: Library hosts talk with author Pam Houston
copy: Pam Houston, author of *Animals Taught Me Everything*, speaks and signs at Wilkinson Public Library Monday, Oct. 26, at 5:30 p.m. The book draws on her experiences with horses, wolves, elephants, and other animals to explore how they model the essentials of living. Houston also wrote *Deep Creek: Finding Hope In The High Country* and lives on a homestead near the Rio Grande headwaters.

title: Chipeta Lodge renews focus on lodging, wellness and community
copy: Chipeta Lodge in Ridgway is refocusing on lodging, spa, and wellness while converting its White Buffalo restaurant into a casual bar with grab-and-go options. Day passes to the pool and spa are now available to locals. Catering for events shifts to Grace & Grit, reviving a partnership from the lodge's 1990s bed-and-breakfast days.

title: A community hub
copy: Kelly and Will Dagostino took over the Sawpit Mercantile in July 2024 and spent their first six months just watching and listening before making changes. They've added espresso, sandwiches, a grab-and-go menu, and free live music while keeping the barbecue program going. When mudslides shut down Highway 145 in July, they kept the doors open, fed stranded travelers until the food ran out, and kept the band playing.

title: County staff discusses housing code updates
copy: San Miguel County held a joint work session to review proposed land use code updates aimed at removing regulatory barriers to housing development, including changes to density rules, new cottage and cohousing definitions, and a 3,000-square-foot cap on free-market homes. Streamlined approval processes would allow smaller projects to move faster through the planning commission.

title: Lady Miners win league XC title
copy: Telluride's girls cross country team claimed the San Juan Basin League title at Saturday's Chicken Creek Challenge north of Mancos, finishing third overall but first among league schools with 59 points. Senior Ruby Cieciuch led the way, placing eighth in 23:29. On the boys' side, junior Daniel Spinei was THS's top finisher at 48th overall.

title: Mountain club announces approval of new trail construction
copy: After nearly a decade of planning, the Telluride Mountain Club has received approval for ~8 miles of new trail and 5.5 miles of rehab, with a $2M price tag. First up: a Mountain Village–to–Valley Floor connector, targeting a late summer 2027 opening. A South Side route from Town Park to Bridal Veil Falls is also in the mix.

title: A modern Mayberry: SMC Sheriff candidate Dan Covault
copy: Dan Covault, appointed San Miguel County Sheriff 16 months ago after 20 years in the office, is now running his first public election. He's added water tanks for fire risk areas, expanded mental health programs, and built a corrections academy. Deep roots here — he's worked the region since his teens.

title: ‘Deep-seated Telluride identity’: SMC Sheriff candidate Lane Masters
copy: Lane Masters, 37, is running for San Miguel County Sheriff — a lifelong goal for the Telluride native and son of retiring 46-year Sheriff Bill Masters. He brings nine years with the Bismarck PD plus current local deputy and sergeant experience. He's focused on staffing and calls disaster preparedness the county's biggest public safety challenge.

title: Native athlete pride: Shiyazh Pete recognized on Indigenous Peoples Day
copy: Shiyazh Pete made history as the first Navajo Nation member to sign with an NFL team, drawing thousands of fans to his Cowboys preseason debut. Now a free agent, he's been back home visiting schools and community events. The story also runs through a long list of Native athletes who've reached the top of their sports going back to Jim Thorpe in 1912.

title: Council members hear housing updates
copy: Telluride's Town-owned rental units sit at a 19% vacancy rate, with two units recently added at Sunnyside and Shandoka. The new Resident Advisory Committee flagged that rental applications are confusing, prompting two help sessions at Wilkinson Library on Oct. 21. The Shandoka redevelopment — 50-60 units plus a 900-vehicle parking structure — moves into HARC and P&Z review that same week.

title: Therapy dogs bring calm and joy to students following shooting at Colorado high school
copy: Two golden Labs, Norene and Polenta, are now permanent fixtures at Evergreen High School near Denver, helping students recover from a September 2024 shooting that wounded two students. The dogs, provided free through the nonprofit Canine Companions, walk the halls and visit classrooms daily. Students took to them quickly — the pair were even crowned prince and princess at homecoming.

title: Protect yourself from seasonal illness
copy: Flu is coming in early and from the West this year, Covid just peaked locally, and mosquito risk stays low here until the first hard frost. San Miguel and Ouray counties are running vaccine clinics for flu, Covid, and RSV — clinics have been filling up fast. Shots are covered by most insurance, and uninsured residents can still get vaccinated.

title: An artistic exploration of water
copy: Telluride Arts HQ is opening a winter group show called "Precipitation" on Nov. 19, running through April 2, with submissions from local and regional artists due Oct. 25. The theme draws on water's deep ties to life in the San Juans — snowpack, runoff, agriculture, mining history. Alongside the show, two local artists will work in-residence at HQ, with visitors able to watch the work being made.

title: Sowing seeds of solace
copy: A remembrance garden is taking shape along the River Trail east of Town Park, created to give people a quiet place to sit with grief in a town better known for festivals. Three benches funded by the Thomas Albert Moore Foundation are in, and a "wind phone" is planned. A dedication ceremony is set for Oct. 27.

title: BOCC approves fee waiver for Ilium Valley housing
copy: San Miguel County commissioners waived roughly $4,000 in planning application fees for Mountain Village's Ilium Valley affordable housing project, which aims to build up to 49 deed-restricted units across two sites. Nonprofit developer Rural Homes Colorado is on board, with Phase 1 groundbreaking targeted for fall 2027 and first move-ins toward end of 2028.

title: Full interviews with both San Miguel County Commissioner candidates
copy: Two candidates — Paul Reich and Dylan Brooks — are vying for San Miguel County Commissioner, each focused on housing and affordability. Reich wants to reverse the livability decline before it's too late; Brooks favors vacant-home tax incentives modeled on Utah's approach. Both see the next four years as pivotal for the region's middle class.

title: Among the best at PantherFest
copy: Telluride junior Speck placed sixth at PantherFest in 20:08, finishing close to the Western Slope's top runners, while three San Juan Basin athletes cracked the overall top 10. The Lady Miners placed eighth as a team, with three juniors finishing nearly side by side in 83rd, 85th, and 87th. The boys' soccer team, ranked No. 1 in 2A, rolled to a 7-0 halftime lead over Caprock Academy.

title: EcoAction, SMPA bring energy updates to Norwood trustees
copy: EcoAction Partners funded six energy efficiency projects in Norwood this year totaling nearly $50,000, covering heat pumps, windows, and EV infrastructure. Their free CARE program has weatherized over 300 homes since 2016. SMPA also completed a long-planned link letting the Nucla and Norwood substations back each other up.

title: Knocking out noxious weeds is everyone’s job
copy: Landowners in the West End of Montrose County gathered recently to tackle the Russian olive problem — a Class C noxious weed so entrenched it's essentially swallowing fencelines and ditches around Nucla. Colorado law requires weed management on private property, and San Miguel County offers cost-share funding for herbicides. Free plant ID help is available through the county vegetation office.

title: CHALKBOARD, week of Oct. 8-14
copy: Norwood's Homecoming week ran Oct. 9-10 with a parade, pep assembly, volleyball, football, bonfire, and a dance. The weekly Chalkboard also lists late-September and early-October birthdays, school events, and standing community meetings and services including the farmers market, food pantry, and senior meals.

title: Hurricane Simon strengthens to a Category 2 storm, the National Hurricane Center says
copy: Hurricane Simon strengthened to Category 2 and is expected to hit Mexico's Jalisco coast as a major storm this weekend, bringing dangerous flooding and mudslides. Jalisco suspended classes, began evacuations, and is moving tourists and workers into shelters. Acapulco has already seen flooded streets and swept vehicles — no casualties reported yet.

title: O’Bannon’s to close
copy: O'Bannon's Irish Pub, a Telluride fixture for nearly 40 years, will close December 31 when owners Ann Marie and Randy Fitzpatrick retire. The group behind The Patio upstairs bought the space and plans to open a bar there, but the O'Bannon's name goes with the Fitzpatricks.

title: Exuberant fiddling for an ‘off-season celebration’
copy: Telluride Chamber Music brings the Hanneke Cassel Trio — fiddle, guitar, and five-string fiddle — to The Alibi on Oct. 13 for its third annual "Not Your Average Classical" folk night. Expect Scottish, Cape Breton, and Americana sounds in a casual, one-long-set format with door prizes. It's become a quiet off-season tradition worth knowing about.

title: Old school: County commissioner candidate Dylan Brooks
copy: Nearly lifelong Telluride resident Dylan Brooks, 54, is running for San Miguel County Commissioner, leaning on 50 years in the valley, a background in financial planning, and two terms on the school board. His main focus is housing — he notes his childhood street now has just two occupied homes. He favors property tax incentives for full-time occupancy and points to Lawson Hill as a model worth building on.

title: Fixing a hole: county commissioner candidate Paul Reich
copy: Paul Reich is running for San Miguel County commissioner with housing affordability as his central focus, motivated in part by watching his five adult children struggle to build lives here. He brings 25-plus years of local public and private sector experience, including board work with the Telluride Hospital District and Telluride School District. The Nov. 3 election will determine if he gets the chance to test his ideas.

title: Legals and Public Notices for Oct. 8-14, 2026
copy: The Telluride Housing Authority is holding a lottery for master lease opportunities at two employee housing properties — Virginia Placer IIA and the Boarding House — with applications open October 9–28 at telluride-co.gov. A foreclosure notice has also been filed on a Tomboy Lodge unit. Mountain Village is considering a new tavern liquor license for El Rhino, with a hearing October 15.

title: Commissioners discuss housing impact fees
copy: San Miguel County commissioners reviewed the Employee Housing Impact Fee, which applies to new residential construction in unincorporated areas within the R-1 School District. With single-family homes averaging over $2,500/sq ft, the market-affordability gap sits at $1,112/sq ft. Some locals and a banker raised concerns that the fees aren't spurring deed-restricted units and may be squeezing out mid-range construction.

title: Dylan Brooks for commissioner
copy: Art Goodtimes, a former San Miguel County commissioner of 20 years, is vouching for Dylan Brooks in the current commissioner race. Brooks grew up in Telluride.

title: Dan Covault for sheriff
copy: Dan Covault is running for re-election as San Miguel County Sheriff against Lane Masters. Covault worked his way up through the department — dispatcher, jail, deputy, investigator, under-sheriff — and received statewide recognition for a major criminal investigation near Norwood. A local letter-writer endorses him based on experience and community knowledge.

title: Masters will rebuild sheriff's office
copy: A retired San Miguel County reserve deputy is raising concerns about staffing and morale at the sheriff's office, saying close to half the patrol deputies have resigned since Dan Covault was appointed interim sheriff in June 2025. The letter also questions the timing of license-plate-reader account cancellations the day before a public records request arrived. The writer backs Lane Masters for sheriff in November.
letterAuthor: John Kirkendoll San Miguel County Reserve, Deputy Sheriff (Retired)

title: Feasible?
copy: The Town of Telluride is moving forward on two large development proposals — roughly 220–240 units at Carhenge and a 900-space underground parking structure with 50–60 units at Lot L — while consultant fees have reached approximately $2.2 million. A community member is raising questions about whether full feasibility, financing, and construction cost analyses have been publicly presented before further commitments are made.

title: No on Props 134 and 135
copy: This is an opinion letter urging a "No" vote on Colorado Propositions 134 and 135. The writer, who identifies as a nurse and mother, argues the measures would shift medical and sports-participation decisions away from families and toward government oversight.

title: If 5A fails, here's what it could cost
copy: Ballot issue 5A would raise about $2.7 million a year for Telluride schools — roughly 13% of district revenue — at a cost of $117 per year per $1 million of home value. The district has already cut 11% of its staff; if 5A fails, cuts could reach 38–66%. Colorado's funding formula changes, not local decisions, created the shortfall.

title: A guide to measures on the November state ballot
copy: Colorado voters face 14 statewide ballot measures this November, including seven propositions that would establish new state law if passed by a simple majority. A San Miguel County official breaks down four of them — covering fentanyl penalties, human trafficking sentencing, school sports eligibility, and gender-affirming surgery for minors — noting where the County Commissioners took formal positions.

title: For Anna
copy: The Brown family — whose parents Scott and Karen founded the Telluride Times 45 years ago — have shared a tribute to their sister Anna Brown, who passed away July 10. Anna grew up in a household defined by an open door, a full table, and deep roots in this valley's early days. She returned to Telluride not out of habit but because what was here was genuinely hers.

title: Magic at the equinox
copy: The San Juans shift toward winter gradually — earlier shadows, quieter creeks, hummingbirds gone. Locals tend to mark it without thinking: moving livestock, picking the last tomatoes, digging out snow tires. The mountains don't resist the turning, and neither do most people here.

title: The happening
copy: Spring soccer in Cortez, a late-season snowstorm on the pass, a summer of swim meets, wildflowers, peaches, and a nearby wildfire — the seasons turned as they do up here. September's low tube clouds are back in the valley, burning off by mid-morning. The dirt's grippy, skis aren't far off.

title: Clarity
copy: Fall in the San Juans brings that sharp, crystalline air where elk bugles carry across the ridges and the views stretch forever — a kind of clarity that's hard to find anywhere else. The writer sets that against a murkier backdrop: the fast-moving world of AI and synthetic biology, where the risks are real but hard to see or name. The mountains stay legible; the wider world, less so.

title: Telluride Foundation to host social media workshop
copy: The Telluride Foundation is hosting a free social media workshop for local nonprofits on Oct. 27, 11 a.m.–12:30 p.m., at Wilkinson Public Library (also available via Zoom). Two local communications professionals will cover practical strategies and common myths around managing social media for mission-driven organizations.

title: Residential composting now available in Mountain Village
copy: Mountain Village residents can now add composting to their Bruin Waste pickup — food scraps and organics diverted from the landfill. Sign up by calling (970) 864-7531 or at bruinwaste.com/compost.

title: Did you know that puppies grow?
copy: Puppies get adopted fast at the local shelter, but they're also the most returned — often when they've grown into adult dogs. Second Chance Humane Society is asking people to think long-term before adopting. Riley, returned as an adult after being adopted as a pup, is currently available.

title: Boomin’ and broomin’
copy: Telluride's volleyball team swept Dove Creek 25-10, 25-22, 25-21 on the road October 2nd, following a Tuesday win at Norwood. The Lady Miners won all three sets, with strong serving and kills from Noel, Fenton, and both Aplins. Telluride moves to 6-9 overall, 3-3 in San Juan Basin play.

title: Cliff Allred features at West End Stories & Poems
copy: Cliff Allred — a Naturita native, cancer survivor, and library employee — will share stories of near-death experiences, ghosts, and unexplained encounters at the Naturita Community Library on Oct. 8 at 6 p.m. The free, all-ages West End Stories & Poems event runs monthly and welcomes the community to share their own stories.

title: Let your freak flag fly
copy: The Not So Young People's Theater brings "Shrek the Musical" to the Sheridan Opera House October 8–11, with 27 performers who've been rehearsing since August. The mixed-age cast includes families, couples, and siblings performing together. Tickets and info through the Sheridan Arts Foundation.

title: Fleeting ‘Birds of Passage’
copy: Telluride Arts is showing "Birds of Passage" at the historic Transfer Warehouse — large papier-mache and cardboard bird sculptures made by artist NVD (Nirali Desai) during a residency at Steeprock Joinery in Sawpit. The pieces are built to deteriorate in the elements, and with recent rain and wind, their run may end before the listed Nov. 8 close date. Nightly video projection runs 7–10 p.m.

title: SOS: ‘Help us protect the quality of our schools’
copy: Telluride R-1 faces a 17% state budget cut starting in 2027-28, and Question 5A on the November ballot would offset that loss through a local mill levy increase costing about $115 per $1M of assessed property value. Programs like Dual Immersion, AP courses, ski PE, and athletics could be reduced without it. Not everyone agrees — at least one local official argues enrollment has dropped enough that staffing cuts could cover the gap instead.

title: A county to come home to
copy: A San Miguel County commissioner candidate lays out his platform ahead of October ballots: housing production, shoulder-season economic diversification, growth paying its own way, and better coordination between the county, towns, and districts. Paul Reich is the Democratic candidate for District 2.

title: Town council upholds Carhenge lot consolidation
copy: Town council voted 3-1 to uphold P&Z's approval of combining two Backman Village lots into a single 4.1-acre parcel for the Carhenge site. The lot consolidation alone doesn't greenlight any development — future proposals still go through standard review. Neighboring residents and the Chair 7 Coalition had appealed the decision.

title: Supreme Court weighs local governments' climate change lawsuits against oil and gas companies
copy: The Supreme Court heard arguments over whether Boulder, Colorado can sue Suncor and ExxonMobil in state court for climate-related damages — part of a wave of similar suits nationwide. Justices seemed divided, with a possible tie given Alito's recusal. A deadlock would leave Colorado's ruling standing, letting the Boulder case proceed.

title: A guide to measures on the November state ballot (Part 1)
copy: Colorado's November ballot includes 14 statewide amendments and propositions, seven of them constitutional changes requiring 55% approval to pass. The first batch covers immigration reporting requirements, natural gas rights, hunting and fishing rights, and mail ballot ID rules. San Miguel County commissioners have weighed in on several measures — details and a full summary document are linked in the piece.

title: Willkommen once again
copy: Mountain Village is expanding Oktoberfest to three days this year — Oct. 9–11 — after a one-day run last year. Heritage Plaza becomes the hub Saturday, with a beer garden, festival tent, oompah bands, family activities, and a Bavarian Market. It wraps Sunday with brunch at Lumière and an adult beverage tasting.

title: Applications Open for 2026/2027 Temporary Winter Community Housing Program
copy: (October 8, 2026) – The Town of Telluride is accepting applications for its Temporary Winter Community Housing program for the 2026/2027 winter season. The program provides seasonal housing in Town Park for eligible workers employed in the Telluride area.

DMV Services available in Egnar 11/18
copy: Attention, West Enders! The DMV will be coming to visit on Wednesday, November 18th, at the Firehouse in Egnar. No appointment necessary. Mark your calendars and save yourself a drive, we'll see you there! Questions? 970-728-3954.

title: Ballot Delivery Delay
copy: Due to an error within the United States Postal Service, delivery of some election mail ballots has been delayed. We understand that receiving your ballot on time is important, and we apologize for the inconvenience and concern this delay may cause.

title: Tomboy Road Now Open
copy: The Town of Telluride has completed their project that necessitated the closure of Lower Tomboy Road. The road is now open again.
